headline: Parent group approval for use of the district name and logo, revisions to Fiscal 924 cash policy, and Students 536 fundraising policy.
summary: The committee will vote on adding one parent group that may use the district name and logo. It will also review proposed changes to the cash policy and discuss the fundraising policy and minimum wage.

Review of the district's minimum wage, requested at the September 14, 2026 meeting (informational only)

the opportunity to address the board.  All people wishing to speak will have up to three (3)

FISCAL            
 924 CASH IN SCHOOL BUILDINGS 
  
[DM: Cash in School Buildings] 
  
Monies collected by school employees and by student treasurers shall be handled with prudent 
business procedures. All monies collected shall be receipted, accounted for, and deposited 
periodically, but not less than weekly. 
In no case shall monies be left overnight in schools, except in safes provided for safekeeping of 
valuables, and even then, not to exceed more than a nominal amount. All vending machines 
shall be emptied of cash periodically, but not less than weekly. All schools shall provide for 
making bank deposits after regular banking hours in order to avoid leaving money in school 
overnight. All schools shall make bank deposits as needed to avoid leaving money in 
schools overnight. This policy shall be well publicized to deter burglary attempts. 
  
History: Revised From 2000, 6/5/24 
  
First Reading Policy Committee: June 5, 2024 October 21, 2026 
  
Second Reading and BOSC Adoption: June 24, 2024 October 26, 2026

Students 
536 FUND RAISING ACTIVITIES 
[JJE: Fund Raising Activities] 
 
Purpose 
The Board recognizes that students, parent/ teacher organizations, athletic groups, staff, booster 
organizations and others may wish to conduct fundraising activities to support Manchester School District 
programs, activities, teams and schools. 
 
Since the general public may  view fundraising associated with a District school, team, club or program as 
being endorsed by the Manchester School District, all fundraising activities require the prior approval of the 
Superintendent  or designee. 
 
Fundraising activities covered by this policy include, but are not limited to:  
 GoFundMe, Donors Choose or similar online fundraising platforms;  
 Cookie dough, candles, books, calendars, restaurant/vendor discount cards and other merchandise; 
 Raffles or auctions 
 Sponsorships;  
 Walk-a-thons or read-a-thons, and similar activities; and, 
 Any other type of solicitation conducted on behalf of a District school, team, program, club or 
organization.  
 
This policy shall not apply to bake sales where the anticipated revenue will not exceed five hundred dollars 
($500.00).  
 
Crowd-funding by employees on behalf of the District is governed by policy Fiscal 909: Crowd Funding. 
 
The Superintendent shall have the authority to impose conditions, limitations or restrictions on such 
fundraising activities in addition to the requirements of this policy as is deemed warranted or as dictated by 
accepted accounting standards and practices.  
 
  
10
Fundraising Requirements 
The following requirements apply to all fundraising activities: 
1. Student Participation   
 No student will be mandated to fundraise.   
 Students may not be penalized or sanctioned for choosing to not participate in fund-raising. 
 Individual student fundraising quotas are prohibited. 
 Students may not personally profit from fundraising activities. 
 
2. Incentives 
 No cash incentives may be paid to any student, employee, coach, advisor or family member in 
connection with fundraising activities. 
 Non-Cash incentives may not exceed $50 in value. 
 Prize cards, cash grabs, cash payouts, commissions or similar incentives are prohibited. 
 Fundraising proceeds may not be used for end of the year gifts, cash or gift cards for staff or 
coaches. 
 
3. Handling of Funds 
 All proceeds generated from such fundraising shall be deposited in compliance with Fiscal 924: 
Cash in School Buildings. Cash and checks must be secured as soon as possible and deposited 
within 24 hours of receipt whenever practicable.  (Please see Athletic Boosters, PTG, PTO, PTA 
section below.) 
 Fundraising money may not be stored in an unsecured area.   
 Access to funds should be limited to authorized individuals. 
 To the extent that the fundraising activities involve the sale of any merchandise, 
restaurant/vendor discount cards, books, or any other thing of material value, a record shall be 
kept, to include: 
a. The specific amount or number of items received by each individual engaged in such 
fundraising; 
b. Total amount or number of items sold; 
c. Total number of items d. The amount of money collected; and, 
d. Any merchandise or money that remains unaccounted for. 
 
4. Personal Retention of Funds or Property 
 
No employee or student or organization associated with the Manchester School District shall be allowed to 
personally retain any item or proceeds secured or generated from such fundraising without the prior 
disclosure and approval of the Superintendent or his/her designee. 
11
5. Vendor Compensation 
 
To the extent any individual, company, vendor or sponsor receive any of the proceeds (remuneration) from 
such fundraising activities, the terms and conditions for the receipt of such remuneration (and amount if 
known) shall be fully disclosed before approval by the Superintendent or designee. 
 
6. Final Accounting 
 
At the conclusion of any fundraising activity, a full accounting shall be made to the Superintendent or the 
designee.  The accounting must include:  
 Total amount of money raised; 
 Any payments made to any vendors, individuals or third parties from the proceeds;  
 Expenses; 
 The net amount of the proceeds received by the Manchester School District or program; and 
 Any unresolved discrepancies involving money or merchandise. 
 
Approval and Oversight  
 
1. Athletic Fundraising 
 
For Athletics related funding raising, the Building Principal or his/her designee shall be responsible for 
ensuring compliance with this policy and any additional requirements established by the Superintendent. 
 
The coach or adviser is responsible for the day-to-day collection, tracking, and bookkeeping of funds 
associated with the fundraiser. 
 
2. Non-Athletic fundraising 
 
For non-athletic related fundraising, the principal of the school receiving the primary benefit of the 
fundraising, or such other person as may be designated by the Superintendent, shall responsible for 
ensuring compliance with this policy and any terms and conditions imposed by the Superintendent. 
 
3. Fundraising Records 
 
The Principal shall maintain a file of all approved fundraisers. 
 
A separate record shall also be maintained at the Superintendent’s office. 
12
4. Authority to Deny Fundraising 
 
The Superintendent shall have the authority to deny any fundraising activity he/she determines to be 
inappropriate or inconsistent with the shared community values of the Manchester School District. 
 
Any contract entered into without the express permission of the Superintendent is void. 
 
Fundraisers Involving Cards, Books, Calendars, Merchandise or Similar Items  
 
To the extent that the fundraising activities involve the sale of any merchandise, restaurant/vendor discount 
cards, books, or any other thing of material value, a record shall be kept as to the specific amount or number 
of items received by each individual engaged in such fundraising and total amount or number of items sold 
and/or returned by each individual engaged in such fundraising. The following steps must be in place: 
 
1. Written Fundraising Plan 
 
A detailed fundraising plan must be submitted to the Building Principal or Superintendent or designee before 
the fundraiser begins.  The plan must include: 
 
 The purpose of the fundraiser; 
 What will be sold; 
 dates of the fundraising event(s),  
 The company or vendor partnering for the fundraiser;  
 How merchandise will be distributed; 
 How funds will be collected and tracked; 
 Any vendor fees or compensation; 
 Any proposed incentives; and, 
 All relevant information provided by the fundraising company or vendor. 
 
2. Use of Fundraising proceeds 
 
All money collected from any fundraiser must  benefit  the approved student program, team, group or 
activity.  There can be no payoffs for participation from vendors to students and/or coaches/advisers. 
 
 
 
13
3. Cash Handling 
 
All money that is collected (cash and checks) must be secured as soon as possible and deposited within 24 
hours of receipt. Funds must be kept in a secured location that should have limited access to others. 
All cash and checks collected through these fundraisers shall be handled in accordance with the Handling of 
Funds requirements contained in this policy, including the requirement that funds be secured promptly and 
deposited within 24 hours whenever practicable.  (Please see Athletic Boosters, PTG, PTO, PTA section 
below.) 
 
4. Individual Student Tracking 
 
Each group or team must establish a bookkeeping plan of how money collection will be tracked for each 
student. This system must document: 
 
 How many cards or items are being sold by each student;  
 How many were returned; 
 The amount collected; and,  
 Any items or funds that remain unaccounted for. 
 
5. Prohibited Incentives 
 
No prize cards, cash grabs, cash payouts and similar promotions etc. are permitted under any 
circumstances.  
 
Students may not profit individually from the sales of any fundraising items.  
 
Fundraising proceeds may not be used for end of the year "gifts/ gift cards"  for  staff or coaches with these 
funds. 
 
6. Vendor Expectations 
 
Teams/groups must  ensure the fundraising vendors understand and agree to comply with District 
fundraising requirements before the fundraiser begins. 
 
7. Student and Family Guidance 
 
14
Clear guidance must be provided to students and families regarding fundraising expectations before the 
fundraiser begins. 
 
Students must not be directed or encouraged to sell door-to-door.  
 
Students should instead be encouraged to sell to family members, friends and other known contacts. 
 
Participation in fundraising remains voluntary. 
 
8. Coach or Adviser Responsibility 
 
The coach or adviser is responsible for the collection, tracking and bookkeeping of the funds relative to the 
fundraising of their program. 
 
9. Contracts 
 
No coach, adviser, employee, volunteer, or other individual may sign a fundraising contract with any vendor 
on behalf of the Manchester School District.  
 
All such contracts should be processed through the Superintendent’s office or their designee. 
 
Any contract entered into without the express written consent of the Superintendent is not authorized by the 
district.   
 
10. Fundraising Exceeding $5,000 
 
Any fundraiser collecting over $5,000 should comply with Fiscal 928: Gifts Donations for a public hearing. 
 
Athletic Boosters/Parent Teacher Groups (PTG)/ Parent Teacher Organizations (PTO)/ Parent 
Teacher Associations (PTA)  
 
Athletic Boosters, Booster clubs, PTGs, PTOs, PTAs and other organizations fundraising with students of 
the Manchester School District and on behalf of programs or schools in the Manchester School District will 
enter in a Memorandum of Understanding with the School District at the start of each school year to outline 
expectations and obligations.  
 
The MOU shall outline fundraising expectations and responsibilities. 
15
Organizations covered by this section must comply with applicable provisions of this policy whenever District 
students participate in fundraising activities.  This MOU shall  include any proposed crowd-funding 
campaigns expected throughout the year, and may be amended as necessary for an unanticipated 
campaigns started during the school year. 
 
Organizations covered by this section must comply with applicable provisions of this policy when District 
students participate in fundraising. 
 
Anticipated Fundraising Activities 
 
The MOU shall identify, to the extent reasonably known, anticipated fundraising activities and proposed 
crowdfunding campaigns for the school year. 
 
Unanticipated Fundraising Opportunities 
 
An organization may propose a fundraising activity that was not anticipated or identified when the 
annual MOU was completed. 
 
Before beginning an unanticipated fundraising activity involving District students or conducted on 
behalf of a District school, team, program, or activity, the organization shall provide written notice to 
the Building Principal or designee. 
 
The notice shall include: 
 The nature of the proposed fundraiser; 
 The purpose for which the funds will be raised; 
 The anticipated dates; 
 Whether District students will participate; 
 Any vendor, sponsor, or third party involved; 
 Any proposed incentives; and 
 Other information reasonably necessary for the District to determine compliance with this 
policy. 
 
16
The Building Principal or designee shall review the proposed activity. 
If the fundraiser is consistent with the existing MOU and District policy, the MOU may be amended or 
supplemented in writing to include the fundraiser. 
 
If the proposed fundraiser creates additional obligations for the District, involves a contract on 
behalf of the District, presents financial or safety concerns, or otherwise falls outside the scope of 
the existing MOU, the activity must be reviewed and approved by the Superintendent or designee 
before it begins. 
 
No unanticipated fundraising activity involving District students may begin until the required review 
and any necessary amendment, supplement, or approval have been completed. 
 
Ownership and Use of Fundraising Proceeds 
 
District-Conducted Fundraising 
All fundraising proceeds, including money, purchases, merchandise, and other assets or physical items 
obtained through fundraising conducted by the District, its schools, teams, programs, clubs, or student 
groups, shall be considered assets of the District or the applicable District program. 
 
Such proceeds must be used for the purpose for which the fundraiser was approved. 
 
When the original purpose has been fulfilled, exhausted, or is no longer available, remaining funds shall 
revert to the student activities fund or another appropriate District fund as designated by the Building 
Principal or designee. 
 
Independent Organizations 
Funds raised by an Athletic Booster, booster club, PTG, PTO, PTA, or similar independent organization shall 
remain the assets of that organization and shall be held and disbursed by its governing board in accordance 
with the organization’s charitable purpose, governing documents, and applicable state and federal law. 
 
Independent organizations shall clearly state the intended purpose of each fundraising appeal. 
 
If funds raised exceed the amount needed for the stated purpose, or if the stated purpose has been fulfilled 
or is no longer available, the organization’s governing board shall determine the appropriate use of the 
17
remaining funds consistent with its charitable purpose, governing documents, donor restrictions, and 
applicable law. 
 
When the fundraising appeal was specifically intended to benefit a District school, team, program, activity, or 
group of students, the organization should consult with the Building Principal or designee regarding an 
alternative use that reasonably supports the same or a similar District-related purpose. 
 
Donated Funds and Property 
Money, merchandise, equipment, or other property donated by an independent organization to the 
Manchester School District, and accepted by the District in accordance with Fiscal 928: Gifts/Donations, 
shall become an asset of the District upon acceptance. 
 
Once accepted, donated funds or property shall be administered in accordance with applicable District 
policies. 
 
 
References: 
 
Fiscal 924: Cash in School Buildings 
Fiscal 909: Crowd Funding Policy 
Fiscal 928: Gifts Donations

First Reading  Policy:  October 21, 2026 
Second Reading and Approval BOSC:  October 26, 2026

The Building Principal or designee shall review the proposed activity. 
If the fundraiser is consistent with the existing MOU and District policy, the MOU may be amended or 
supplemented in writing to include the fundraiser. 
 
If the proposed fundraiser creates additional obligations for the District, involves a contract on 
behalf of the District, presents financial or safety concerns, or otherwise falls outside the scope of 
the existing MOU, the activity must be reviewed and approved by the Superintendent or designee 
before it begins. 
 
No unanticipated fundraising activity involving District students may begin until the required review 
and any necessary amendment, supplement, or approval have been completed. 
 
Ownership and Use of Fundraising Proceeds 
 
District-Conducted Fundraising 
All fundraising proceeds, including money, purchases, merchandise, and other assets or physical items 
obtained through fundraising conducted by the District, its schools, teams, programs, clubs, or student 
groups, shall be considered assets of the District or the applicable District program. 
 
Such proceeds must be used for the purpose for which the fundraiser was approved. 
 
When the original purpose has been fulfilled, exhausted, or is no longer available, remaining funds shall 
revert to the student activities fund or another appropriate District fund as designated by the Building 
Principal or designee. 
 
Independent Organizations 
Funds raised by an Athletic Booster, booster club, PTG, PTO, PTA, or similar independent organization shall 
remain the assets of that organization and shall be held and disbursed by its governing board in accordance 
with the organization’s charitable purpose, governing documents, and applicable state and federal law. 
 
26
Clean Copy 
 
Independent organizations shall clearly state the intended purpose of each fundraising appeal. 
 
If funds raised exceed the amount needed for the stated purpose, or if the stated purpose has been fulfilled 
or is no longer available, the organization’s governing board shall determine the appropriate use of the 
remaining funds consistent with its charitable purpose, governing documents, donor restrictions, and 
applicable law. 
 
When the fundraising appeal was specifically intended to benefit a District school, team, program, activity, or 
group of students, the organization should consult with the Building Principal or designee regarding an 
alternative use that reasonably supports the same or a similar District-related purpose. 
 
Donated Funds and Property 
Money, merchandise, equipment, or other property donated by an independent organization to the 
Manchester School District, and accepted by the District in accordance with Fiscal 928: Gifts/Donations, 
shall become an asset of the District upon acceptance. 
 
Once accepted, donated funds or property shall be administered in accordance with applicable District 
policies.

The Board recognizes that students, parent/ teacher organizations, athletic groups, staff and 
others may wish to engage in fundraising activities to support the programs or offerings provided 
by the Manchester School District.  
Since the general public may see such fundraising efforts as carrying the endorsement of the 
Manchester School District, all such fundraising activities require the prior approval of the 
Superintendent and/or his/her designee.

GoFundMe, Donors Choose or other similar web pages, cookie dough, candles, raffles, auctions, 
restaurant/vendor discount cards, book sales, sponsorships, walk or read-a-thons, or any other 
type of solicitation. This policy shall not apply to bake sales where the anticipated revenue will 
not exceed five hundred dollars ($500.00). Crowd-funding by employees on behalf of the 
District is governed by Fiscal 909.

such fundraising activities in addition to the requirements of this policy as is deemed warranted 
or as dictated by accepted accounting standards and practices. Notwithstanding, the following 
conditions shall apply to all such fundraising activities:

raising.

or student of the Manchester School District (including family members) in recognition of 
such fundraising activities.
